items.title: آنچه گذشت؛ سنتکام: نیروهای آمریکایی یک کشتی تجاری را در دریای عمان هدف قرار دادند
items.summary: سنتکام اعلام کرد که یک کشتی تجاری را به دلیل تلاش برای نقض محاصره دریایی ایران در دریای عمان هدف قرار داد و از حرکت بازداشت. به گفته این فرماندهی، یک هواپیمای نظامی آمریکا پس از هشدار به خدمه کشتی «هودا»، با شلیک مهمات هدایت‌شونده به بخش انتهایی آن، کشتی را از حرکت انداخت. سنتکام پیش‌تر نیز از تشکیل کارگروهی ویژه برای محدود کردن جابه‌جایی تسلیحات پیشرفته و دیگر اقلام تحریمی ایران از طریق مرزهای زمینی و دریای خزر خبر داده بود. این فرماندهی می‌گوید از ماه ژوئیه تاکنون ۱۴۷ کشتی تجاری را وادار به تغییر مسیر کرده و پنج کشتی دیگر را از حرکت بازداشته است.

items.title: ترامپ: در صورت پیشرفت در مذاکرات ازسرگیری حملات به ایران بسیار بعید است
items.summary: دونالد ترامپ، رئیس‌جمهور آمریکا، می‌گوید در صورت پیشرفت مذاکرات درباره برنامه هسته‌ای ایران و بازگشایی تنگه هرمز، احتمال این که ناچار شود دستور ازسرگیری جنگ با ایران را صادر کند، «بسیار بعید» است. عباس عراقچی، وزیر خارجه ایران هم پیش‌تر گفته بود که «پیشنهاد دو روزه» ایران برای باز شدن تنگه هرمز در صورت برآورده شدن شرایطش همچنان روی میز است و افزود کاخ سفید باید در این باره تصمیم بگیرد.

items.summary_original: White House Deputy Chief of Staff Richard Walters, a longtime ally of outgoing White House Chief of Staff Susie Wiles, is leaving the Trump administration following President Donald Trump's decision to replace Wiles with Stephen Miller. Miller confirmed Walters' departure in a statement to Fox News, describing him as an "invaluable member" of the White House who will continue to assist the administration from the outside. "Richard has been an invaluable member of the White House and has helped deliver some of the Administration’s biggest victories. While he will be leaving us, Richard will continue to help from the outside as we continue to work with all of our strength to deliver for President Trump and his courageous fight to Save America," Miller said. This is a developing story. Please check back for updates.

items.summary_original: When an insurgent's bullet shattered his arm in combat, Republican Florida Lt. Gov. Jay Collins did not wait around for an evacuation team; the Green Beret performed emergency surgery on himself to save the limb. After the midterms that Gov. Ron DeSantis called a "near extinction-level" event for Republicans, Collins sees a national GOP lying bloodied on the field. He advises his battered and beaten party to show the same refusal to die, and get up like a warrior. "Where we go from here is up to us as a Republican Party," Collins, dubbed the "Chuck Norris of Florida politics" by DeSantis, told Fox News Digital in an interview just days after the midterm "bloodbath." "This can be a definitive death blow if we allow it to be, but I believe in what we stand for." he continued. "I believe in our Constitution. I believe in our founding fathers' vision. I believe that God blessed this nation. I think we have to knuckle down, learn, apply this, and we have come out with a relentless dedication and fury to focus on what matters: To lead our state, to lead our country, and be what we need to be for the American people. items.summary_original: Republican Alaska Gov. Mike Dunleavy admits his own state's voting system is "very confusing," and warned that the close race between Democratic Senate nominee Mary Peltola and incumbent Republican Sen. Dan Sullivan will not be determined for days, if not weeks. "It's very close, the numbers," Dunleavy told WABC Radio's "The Cats Roundtable" on Sunday, noting key dates for ballot dumps will be Friday, Nov. 13, and Wednesday, Nov. 18, when "another big batch of votes will come in." "It's a slow system up here in Alaska," he admitted, acknowledging that "we've got quite an issue up here." "A big batch of votes will come and that'll really determine, you know, who's going to have the lead." ALASKA, MISSISSIPPI SENATE RACES SEPARATED BY RAZOR-THIN VOTE MARGINS Peltola, currently with 48.17% support, leads by just 637 votes in Alaska's ranked-choice voting system that has not dropped any new vote tallies for days. Election Day was Tuesday, Nov. 3, and if no candidate gets 50% support as the No. 1 choice by Nov. 25, the results go to rounds of ranked-choice candidates on the second and third choices. "It is very confusing," Dunleavy said. "That was also on the ballot, to actually repeal that voting scheme that was put in place here just a couple years ago, and so it's confusing, 100%." items.summary_original: A GOP lawmaker in Texas is seeking to limit some of the incoming governor's powers after Democrats flipped the state blue in Tuesday's election. Republican Texas state Rep. Brian Harrison on Wednesday publicly urged outgoing Gov. Greg Abbott to convene a special session to "rein in" the governor's executive emergency powers before Democratic Gov.-elect Gina Hinojosa takes office. " Republicans lost last night, but Democrats were not sworn in," Harrison wrote in a lengthy statement posted on X. "We still have total power in Texas, and we must act like it by using the remaining ten weeks to restore separation of powers and limit the emergency powers that Governor-Elect Hinojosa is set to inherit, that would allow her to destroy liberty in Texas by executive fiat." Harrison also emphasized in the post that he believes Texas governors should not have "unchecked" emergency powers, regardless of their party affiliation. TED CRUZ SAYS 'BLUE TSUNAMI' TOOK OVER TEXAS AFTER DEMOCRATS SWEPT STATEWIDE RACES "Texas should have reined in executive emergency powers when I first demanded it in 2022," Harrison told Fox News Digital on Thursday. "If these are not revoked, Gina Hinojosa will assume not just the powers our state constitution bestows upon a Governor, but will, in effect, inherit nearly all the powers of a dictator. items.summary_original: JERUSALEM — With Iran’s missing-in-action Supreme Leader Ayatollah Mojtaba Khamenei taunting Americans about the "collapse" of the U.S. after the midterm elections, the White House and Middle East experts argue President Donald Trump is positioned to defeat the remnants of the rogue regime. The remaining two years of Trump’s Iran policy have profound implications for his legacy and could lay the foundation for a new Middle East devoid of the region’s worst state sponsor of terrorism, the Islamic Republic of Iran, should Trump pursue new military actions to dislodge Khamenei’s regime, according to experts. Khamenei, who has not been seen in public since a joint U.S.-Israel airstrike killed his father, former Supreme Leader Ali Khamenei , and members of his family, boasted on X following the Republican defeat in the midterms: "The process of the US's collapse has accelerated." A White House spokesperson told Fox News Digital, "The United States is in a very strong position with control of the Strait of Hormuz and the Iranian economy collapsing. items.title: پویش میان دوره ای دموکرات ها راه را برای دور زدن کالج الکترال تا سال 2028 باز می کند.
items.title_original: Democrats’ midterm sweep opens path to bypassing Electoral College by 2028
items.summary: دستاوردهای میان‌دوره‌ای دموکرات‌ها جبهه جدیدی را در مبارزه بر سر نحوه انتخاب رئیس‌جمهور آمریکا باز کرده است - جبهه‌ای که می‌تواند رقابت سال 2028 برای کاخ سفید را تغییر دهد. دموکرات ها اکنون دفتر فرماندار و هر دو مجلس قانونگذاری ایالتی در میشیگان، پنسیلوانیا، ویسکانسین و نوادا را کنترل می کنند. میثاق بین ایالتی رای مردمی ملی که قبلاً توسط 18 ایالت و واشنگتن دی سی تصویب شده است، دارای 222 رأی الکترال است که 48 رأی کمتر از 270 رأی لازم برای اجرایی شدن است. اگر چهار ایالت به آن بپیوندند، مجموع 50 رای الکترال آنها، این توافقنامه را به 272 می رساند و آن را فعال می کند. اگر دموکرات ها در نهایت کنترل هر دو مجلس را در آریزونا به دست آورند، می تواند مجموع را به 283 برساند. رای مردمی ملی (NPV)، سازمان غیرانتفاعی که این قرارداد را نویسندگی کرده است و در حال مبارزه برای تصویب آن است.
items.summary_original: Democrats’ midterm gains have opened a new front in the fight over how America chooses its president — one that could reshape the 2028 race for the White House. Democrats now control the governor’s office and both chambers of the state legislature in Michigan, Pennsylvania, Wisconsin and Nevada. The National Popular Vote Interstate Compact, already enacted by 18 states and Washington, D.C., has 222 electoral votes pledged to it — 48 short of the 270 needed to take effect. If the four states join, their combined 50 electoral votes would push the compact to 272 and activate it. Arizona could push the total to 283 if Democrats ultimately gain control of both chambers there. National Popular Vote (NPV), the nonprofit organization that authored the compact and is campaigning to enact it state by state, says it has identified multiple legislative sponsors in each of the five states whose combined electoral votes could push the compact over the 270-vote threshold. It expects bills to be pre-filed before, or introduced early, in the 2027 legislative sessions. "I am confident we have multiple paths to secure the 48 electoral votes required to deliver what 63% of Americans want," Patrick Rosenstiel, a senior consultant for NPV, told Fox News Digital. VANCE, CRUZ AND DESANTIS DIAGNOSE GOP'S MIDTERM DISASTER AS BATTLE OVER PARTY'S FUTURE BEGINS Under the current electoral system, every state except Maine and Nebraska awards its electoral votes to the candidate who wins the statewide vote

items.summary_original: With Democrats taking control of Congress in the midterm elections, MAGA voters are already sizing up potential successors to President Donald Trump in 2028 — with Vice President JD Vance and Secretary of State Marco Rubio repeatedly emerging as favorites among those interviewed by Fox News Digital. "I like [Rubio]," one American told Fox News Digital. "I like that he's no-nonsense, similar to Trump." "Well, I like JD Vance obviously," another said. "I like Marco Rubio. There's some other ones, too, that are maybe not so much mainstream that are coming up that I like too." TRUMP TOLD DONORS 'WE NEED TO ELECT JD,' SOURCE CONFIRMS, AS HE WEIGHS VANCE OR RUBIO IN 2028 "JD is great too, but Rubio has a little more experience," one said. "He's articulate, he’s well-spoken. He's got good ideas. I just really like him." Fox News Digital spoke with Americans attending a Trump rally in Port Huron, Michigan, as one of Trump’s final stops before Tuesday’s midterms that ended in a stunning blue wave. Fueled by anger over high costs and the war with Iran , Americans voted to oust Trump and his agenda, boosting Democrats to large majorities in the House and Senate. With Democrats looking to rebuke Trump and his allies, Republicans that Fox News Digital spoke with are looking for a presidential candidate to fill in Trump’s "footsteps." "I'm really open to see who can fill Trump's footsteps, not just the next person in line," one told Fox News Digital. FOX NEWS/NORC STUDY: VOTERS LOOK TO 202

items.summary_original: The Democratic Socialists of America (DSA) is taking its message into classrooms, childcare programs and school boards, urging organizers to approach childcare "from a socialist perspective" through initiatives such as Socialist Sprouts, and it's been an initiative for years, a parental-rights watchdog warns. In New York City, the DSA's "Red Sprouts" program held a training session in October 2026 to equip organizers to provide "resistance-driven childcare" at demonstrations, meetings and community events. The training encouraged participants to incorporate political themes into childcare through "radical storytelling," "cooperative games" and age-appropriate discussions. "There's been a real influx in enthusiasm and their ability and desire to recruit and grow their movement," American Parents Coalition leader Alleigh Marré told Fox News Digital. "What's particularly concerning and insidious, is their direct efforts to apply that to not just adults, but to youth." Marré said the American Parents Coalition is working to equip parents with resources to identify and question political activism in schools, including through its "Lookout" initiative. items.summary_original: The owners of a multigenerational cattle ranch say they are facing an "existential threat" after the Washington state Department of Ecology fined them hundreds of thousands of dollars over their stockwater ponds, and they are warning the case could have substantial implications nationwide. The department fined Wade and Teresa King, owners of King Ranch in Grant and Douglas counties, $267,540 in 2023 for allegedly damaging regulated wetlands by digging ponds to provide water for their ranching operations. The Kings argue the areas, which they were ordered to restore, are long-standing stockwater ponds for their livestock, not regulated wetlands. The Kings, who have been trying to get their case in front of a jury, told Fox News Digital that, not only is their financial stability at stake, so are the rights of other ranchers. "Losing this fight would be an existential threat," Wade said. "I don't know how we would recover from that, to be honest with you." HOW A LOBSTERMAN'S PRIVACY FIGHT REACHED SCOTUS — AND COULD RIPPLE FAR BEYOND THE WATER: 'AIN'T OVER YET' When the Kings were first hit with the fines and restoration orders, they immediately set out to challenge them. items.title_original: New Jersey town reveals staggering $26M theft days after election, sparking backlash
items.summary: یکی از شهرستان‌های نیوجرسی پس از اینکه مقامات فاش کردند که 26 میلیون دلار در یک انتقال سیمی جعلی به سرقت رفته است، با واکنش‌های شدید مواجه شده است و ساکنان می‌پرسند که چرا این سرقت گسترده تا بیش از پنج هفته بعد - درست چند روز پس از روز انتخابات - فاش نشد. لیزا کنیریم، شهردار شهر کرنبری، روز جمعه اعلام کرد که شهرداری قربانی یک "سرقت مالی پیچیده" به ارزش تقریبی 26 میلیون دلار شده است. Knierim، یک دموکرات، گفت که انتقال پولی تقلبی در 28 سپتامبر انجام شد، با وجوهی که در ابتدا برای خرید ملک برای انجام تعهدات مسکن مقرون به صرفه شهرستان تعیین شده بود. یک کارگروه متشکل از سازمان‌های مجری قانون محلی، شهرستانی، ایالتی و فدرال، به رهبری اداره پلیس شهرستان و دفتر دادستانی شهرستان میدلسکس، در حال کار است.
items.summary_original: A New Jersey township is facing backlash after officials revealed that $26 million was stolen in a fraudulent wire transfer, with residents questioning why the massive theft wasn't disclosed until more than five weeks later — just days after Election Day. Cranbury Township Mayor Lisa Knierim announced Friday that the municipality had been the victim of a "sophisticated financial theft" involving approximately $26 million. Knierim, a Democrat, said the fraudulent wire transfer took place on Sept. 28, with the funds originally designated for purchasing property to meet the township's affordable housing obligations. A task force involving local, county, state and federal law enforcement agencies, led by the township's police department and the Middlesex County Prosecutor's Office, is working to recover the funds, according to the mayor's statement. CYBERCRIME LOSSES NEAR $21B: 5 WAYS TO PROTECT YOUR MONEY So far, investigators have frozen nearly $17.3 million in assets, leaving approximately $8.7 million outside the reported freeze. The township said the investigation remains active, adding that additional details cannot be released. Knierim's announcement came Nov. 6, three days after the midterm elections and more than five weeks after the theft. Several residents responded to the announcement on the township's Facebook page, questioning the timing of the disclosure and demanding greater transparency from local officials. items.summary_original: Israeli President Isaac Herzog announced Saturday that he has chosen opposition leader Gadi Eisenkot to form the country's next government, handing Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's chief rival the first opportunity to build a coalition following an inconclusive national election. Herzog announced his decision on Nov. 7, but the formal presentation of the mandate is scheduled for Sunday, Nov. 8, at 5 p.m. Israeli time. Eisenkot will then have 28 days to assemble a government, with a possible 14-day extension. The decision could mark a significant step toward ending Netanyahu’s tenure, but it would also launch a difficult round of coalition negotiations, with deep disagreements among parties seeking to replace him. NETANYAHU DEFIES EXIT POLLS AS VOTE SHIFTS IN HIS FAVOR, BUT MAJORITY REMAINS ELUSIVE Following two days of consultations with Israel’s newly elected parliament, Herzog announced Thursday that factions representing 67 of the Knesset’s 120 members had recommended Eisenkot, chairman of the Yashar party, to form the next government. Netanyahu received the backing of 46 lawmakers, while seven members of the ultra-Orthodox United Torah Judaism party declined to endorse either candidate. "The results of the consultations may appear clear," Herzog said in his Nov. 5 statement, but cautioned that competing political demands and vetoes have left the prospects for forming a government uncertain. Trump wore a Dalma suede bomber jacket by Nour Hammour, paired with an Adam Lippes skirt and Manolo Blahnik BB pumps for the occasion, blending her signature polished style with a more relaxed look suited to a college football weekend. The first lady's visit unfolded against a distinctly LSU backdrop, with purple-and-gold tailgating crowds lining the motorcade route and a massive American flag hanging above the stage inside Patrick F. Taylor Hall. LSU cheerleaders flanked Trump during her remarks, and the Tiger mascot presented her with both scholarship checks while wearing a signature "Be Best" T-shirt. "This achievement will give young people from foster care an anchor of stability, a strong educational foundation, and a chance to build a wonderful life," Trump told attendees. items.summary_original: Protesters in France are continuing to demonstrate in Paris and across the nation despite police prohibitions on gatherings in the capital. "These events demonstrated the intention of certain individuals to target the institutions of the Republic, specifically through actions directed against public buildings and State services in order to undermine the foundations of the Republic," the police wrote, according to a Fox News Digital translation of a police order . "That these elements characterize a particular and serious risk to public institutions, agent safety, and the normal functioning of public services during such demonstrations," the statement continued. The Department of Homeland Security (DHS) maintains that ICE complied with lawful court orders and that a judicial release order does not permanently shield individuals from immigration enforcement. "When an illegal alien is ordered released by a judge, that does not immunize the alien from immigration enforcement for all time," DHS said in a statement to Fox News Digital. Of the six dead, four are women and two are men, according to Małopolska Police. Shooting from a moving vehicle, the gunman allegedly targeted people at random, injuring civilians as well as police during the attack on Kraków's bustling Main Square. The perpetrator of the attack was shot and detained by police officers. Rescue services are still working at the scene," MPK S.A., the city's municipal public transport company, wrote in a statement shared to X. Video posted on social media showed people running while gunshots rang out. Police shot and wounded the suspect during a gunfight, and the area is now secured, according to authorities. The suspect, who has only been identified by police as a "citizen of the Republic of Poland," was wearing military-style fatigues and used a military-style rifle to carry out the attack, Katarzyna Cisło, a spokesperson for the Kraków police, told Polish network TVN24. items.summary_original: EXCLUSIVE: A group of Minnesota Republican state lawmakers asked the IRS in August 2019 to "conduct a detailed reexamination" of tax filings by Rep. Ilhan Omar, D-Minn., based on a report from a state board suggesting she filed joint tax returns in 2014 and 2015 with a man she was not legally married to, according to a letter obtained by Fox News Digital. The letter was sent after the Minnesota Campaign Finance and Public Disclosure Board issued a report June 6, 2019, indicating Omar had filed joint tax returns in 2014 and 2015 with Ahmed Hirsi despite being legally married to another man, Ahmed Nur Said Elmi, at the time. The joint tax returns came up during the Minnesota Campaign Finance and Public Disclosure Board’s examination of a $1,500 expense associated with Omar’s campaign committee. The board was investigating whether the expenditure was a legitimate campaign-related expense or whether campaign funds had been used to pay for services that benefited Omar personally. The payment was part of a larger $2,250 reimbursement to the Kjellberg Law Office for legal and other services. items.summary_original: District attorneys and law enforcement unions across California have publicly condemned Gov. Gavin Newsom following his announcement to commute the sentences of 548 death row inmates, a decision one prosecutor called a slap in the face to victims' families. Newsom’s sweeping order to commute the condemned inmates to life in prison without the possibility of parole has drawn intense criticism alongside praise from anti-death penalty advocates. "I think it's all about politics, sadly. Politics is over people in this case, and that's a real sad state of affairs," San Luis Obispo County District Attorney Dan Dow told Fox News Digital. ALABAMA GOVERNOR COMMUTES DEATH SENTENCE AS DOUBTS EMERGE ABOUT EVIDENCE IN MURDER CONVICTION In an open letter detailing his decision, Newsom said California's capital punishment system is fundamentally at odds with the state's principles. "After nearly 30 years in public office, I have come to understand the limits of what government can justly accomplish," Newsom wrote. "I take this action because I firmly believe that state-sanctioned killing is incompatible with California’s values, undermines the foundations of our legal system, and diminishes each of us." POPE LEO DENOUNCES DEATH PENALTY AS 'INADMISSIBLE' AHEAD OF PENTAGON'S PLANNED LIVESTREAMED EXECUTION Upon taking office in 2019, Newsom issued an executive moratorium on capital punishment . items.summary_original: Several Republican lawmakers are fuming over President Donald Trump’s elevation of Stephen Miller to be his chief of staff. The fiercely loyal Miller, who has been with Trump since his first administration, took over for Susie Wiles, who was ousted from the critical role on Thursday. While he has plenty of admirers, his take-no-prisoners style has made him an enemy of Democrats and even some Republicans. "Horrible decision," Rep. Marlin Stutzman, R-Ind., told Fox News Digital Friday after Trump announced his decision. A Republican lawmaker who was granted anonymity to speak candidly described being in "utter disbelief." Tensions were rising against Miller in the wake of Republicans’ terrible performance in Tuesday’s midterm elections . Multiple House Republicans who spoke with Fox News Digital just moments before his promotion said Miller, who spearheads Trump’s immigration policy, should be fired. TRUMP NAMES STEPHEN MILLER NEW WHITE HOUSE CHIEF OF STAFF, REPLACING SUSIE WILES When later asked about his promotion, one House Republican who said Miller should be fired replied simply with a facepalm emoji. Republicans suffered historic losses that saw both the House and Senate fall into Democrats’ hands in the new Congress. Democrats are on pace to win more than 250 seats in the House and at least 54 in the Senate. "Long ago, you predicted that you would win this race by seven points, which, at the time, seemed like a pretty cocky and ill-considered thing to say. Then you won the race by seven points. People are still calling you cocky," podcast host Jon Favreau said during his interview with El-Sayed. "How do you see yourself?" "I think there is a responsibility that we have to engage with [Trump] as the unserious fool that he is," El-Sayed replied. EL-SAYED MOCKS TRUMP, VANCE AND ROGERS IN GLOATING VICTORY SPEECH SIGNALING COMBATIVE TONE IN SENATE El-Sayed’s response sheds light on his view of his own campaign and the tone that he believes Democrats need to adopt to counter Trump’s presence in American politics. It also raises questions of whether El-Sayed’s campaign strategies will yield results in Congress. In his view, Trump has changed the style of acceptable communication. In turn, he accused Democrats of being hesitant to abandon a kind of decorum to fight fire with fire. items.summary_original: Republican control of the Senate could return as soon as the 2028 general election, but only if the party can pull off a series of crucial victories in competitive races, a possibility that seems distant following Tuesday night's devastating Democratic sweep. As of publication, Democrats and independents who caucus with them have secured 54 Senate seats, a total that could grow to as many as 56 pending election calls in Mississippi and Alaska. Assuming Republicans hold the vice presidency in 2028, far from a guarantee, they would need to flip at least four seats during that election cycle to win the Senate back. While there are ample pickup opportunities for Republicans in 2028 if the party can return to its typical national performance benchmarks, several vulnerable GOP-held seats could complicate their efforts to retake the upper chamber. DEMS FLIPS YET ANOTHER SENATE SEAT IN TRUMP COUNTRY AMID SWEEPING GOP UPSETS Iowa Sen. Chuck Grassley, for instance, turned 93 in September and faces a decision about whether to seek another term in 2028, when Republicans will be defending his seat in a state where Democrat Josh Turek just defeated Republican Ashley Hinson by roughly four percentage points. His departure before then could also give Iowa's incoming Democratic governor the opportunity to appoint a temporary replacement. items.summary_original: Some troops have gone a year without hot water. Others are sleeping in their cars to escape barracks without air conditioning. And some are asking for little more than drywall, spackle and paint so they can make repairs themselves. Those are among the conditions Medal of Honor recipient Dakota Meyer says he has encountered while touring military installations on a mission from War Secretary Pete Hegseth : Fix a barracks system plagued by decades of neglect. "I would tell you that there's only a couple that I've seen that are good," Meyer told Fox News Digital in an interview Thursday. DAKOTA MEYER TALKS SERVICE, BLASTS CONTROVERSIAL DESIGN FOR GLOBAL WAR ON TERROR MEMORIAL Meyer, who serves as a senior advisor to the Pentagon's Barracks Task Force, has visited more than eight installations across the Army, Navy, Air Force and Marine Corps since taking on the assignment and plans to visit 30 before the end of the year. "What I thought was gonna be a professional job very quickly turned into personal," Meyer said. At one installation, Meyer recalled asking a 19-year-old service member what she would change about her living conditions if she could "wave a magic wand." items.summary_original: Two socialist mayors were elected in the United States on Tuesday in Los Angeles and Washington, D.C. which means four of the top 20 largest cities in the country have socialist leaders. Los Angeles Councilwoman Nithya Raman, a member of the Democratic Socialists of America (DSA) defeated incumbent Mayor Karen Bass and will take office in December as mayor for the roughly 4 million residents of Los Angeles proper. Also victorious on Tuesday was DSA member Janeese Lewis George, who coasted to victory to become mayor-elect of Washington, D.C., a city of roughly 700,000 residents. The list of socialist mayors in the top 20 most populous U.S. cities stands at four, after George and Raman joined Seattle Mayor Katie Wilson and New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani. DEMOCRATIC SOCIALIST SWEEPS INTO DC MAYOR'S OFFICE, SIGNALS OPENNESS TO WORKING WITH TRUMP In total, the four cities are home to roughly 14 million people. That figure does not include neighboring suburbs, which could still feel the effects of policies enacted within city limits through crime, real estate values and the broader business climate. Problems in a city can spill over into surrounding communities, while suburban residents who work in the city may also be directly affected. Counting the population in the metro areas of those four cities, roughly 44 million people could be affected either positively or negatively by the socialist policies enacted by the four mayors. items.summary_original: President Donald Trump highlighted NASA's ambitious plans to launch its first nuclear-powered spacecraft to Mars within the next two years, reaffirming his administration's push to expand American space exploration and eventually send astronauts to the red planet. Speaking at the UP Summit at Kennedy Space Center in Cape Canaveral, Florida, Trump touted the mission as part of his administration's broader ambitions to expand America's presence beyond Earth. "Within the next two years, NASA will launch the first-ever nuclear-powered spacecraft to Mars ," Trump said. The president described the mission as a step toward eventually sending American astronauts to the planet. TRUMP CALLS ISS CREW FROM HOUSTON TO PRAISE SPACE PIONEERS AND OFFER 'OVAL OFFICE TIME' "We're going to be paving the way for astronauts to plant the Stars and Stripes on the red planet," he said. The planned mission comes as NASA's Artemis program aims to establish a long-term human presence on the moon before eventually sending astronauts to Mars. Earlier this year, astronauts completed a lunar flyby during the Artemis II mission. Artemis III is scheduled to test spacecraft and landing systems in Earth orbit in 2027, while Artemis IV is expected to attempt a lunar landing in early 2028, before the end of Trump's presidential term. items.summary: ابوظبی، امارات متحده عربی — در افتتاحیه بزرگترین کنفرانس انرژی جهان در ابوظبی، هوش مصنوعی در کنار نفت و گاز در کانون توجه قرار گرفت زیرا سام آلتمن، مدیر عامل OpenAI به مقامات ارشد امارات متحده عربی برای اعلام همکاری بزرگی با هدف ورود هوش مصنوعی پیشرفته به صنعت انرژی پیوست. مراسم افتتاحیه ADIPEC 2026 با حضور فاکس نیوز دیجیتال، مقامات ارشد دولتی و رهبران صنعت انرژی را در زمانی گرد هم آورد که جنگ با ایران و اختلال در تنگه هرمز فشار فوق‌العاده‌ای بر عرضه جهانی انرژی وارد کرده است. اما در میان بحث در مورد تولید نفت، مسیرهای کشتیرانی و امنیت انرژی، دکتر سلطان الجابر، وزیر صنعت و فناوری پیشرفته امارات متحده عربی و مدیر اجرایی انرژی دولتی
items.summary_original: ABU DHABI, United Arab Emirates — At the opening of the world's largest energy conference in Abu Dhabi, artificial intelligence took center stage alongside oil and gas as OpenAI CEO Sam Altman joined senior UAE officials for the announcement of a major partnership aimed at bringing advanced AI into the energy industry. The opening ceremony of ADIPEC 2026, attended by Fox News Digital, brought together senior government officials and energy industry leaders at a time when the war involving Iran and disruptions to the Strait of Hormuz have placed extraordinary pressure on global energy supplies. But amid discussions about oil production, shipping routes and energy security, Dr. Sultan Al Jaber, the UAE’s minister of industry and advanced technology and chief executive of state-owned energy giant ADNOC, delivered a different challenge to the technology industry. OIL SQUEEZE TIGHTENS AS IRAN-BACKED ATTACKS CRIPPLE HORMUZ ESCAPE ROUTES "From the moment ChatGPT was born, the world has asked what energy can do for AI. And now, together, we will find out what AI can do for energy," Al Jaber told the audience, introducing a partnership between ADNOC, OpenAI and Abu Dhabi-based technology company G42. The announcement marked a significant step in the UAE’s ambition to become a global center for artificial intelligence, using its energy resources, financial strength and growing partnerships with American technology companies to help shape the industry’s future. items.summary_original: First lady Melania Trump and envoys from both Russia and Ukraine spoke from the White House on Thursday, hailing the ceasefire in the Russian-occupied Oleshky region as a potential "spark" for peace that lasts beyond a temporary regional ceasefire. "We have chosen humanity over war," the first lady said in a White House trilateral news conference with the two warring countries. "Undeniably, the lives of innocent people must transcend the division of war. I hope Oleshky inspires greater peace. Every significant transformation begins with a small spark." "Together, we can create something more enduring than a temporary ceasefire," she added, calling Oleshky "a spark in a world of darkness capable of illuminating the best in humanity." INSIDE MELANIA TRUMP'S SECRET DIPLOMATIC ROLE IN THE RUSSIA-UKRAINE CEASEFIRE DEAL Trump said she became aware of a humanitarian crisis in the region in September and directed her representative, Marc Beckman, to engage with Russia and Ukraine on her behalf. She said both countries agreed to work with her as an "exclusive intermediary" to establish a ceasefire in Oleshky and the surrounding Kherson region, deliver humanitarian aid and create a safe evacuation route for civilians. Her remarks were followed by comments from Russian special envoy Kirill Dmitriev , who said Russian President Vladimir Putin appreciated President Donald Trump’s efforts to stop the fighting. items.summary_original: France deployed 70,000 police officers Thursday as tens of thousands of people took to the streets for nationwide strikes and protests after left-wing groups called for a mobilization. In Paris, the Eiffel Tower was closed; in Lyon, French riot police fired tear gas and charged a group of protesters; and near Toulouse, a high school was set on fire, according to Reuters. "We need to turn up in big numbers on the streets today," the news agency quoted the head of the left-wing CGT union Sophie Binet as saying. The demonstrations come after France was rocked by violent protests in October, which outgoing French President Emmanuel Macron blamed on "ultra-left groups whose aim is to bring down the Republic." FRANCE'S MACRON BLAMES PROTESTS ON 'ULTRA-LEFT GROUPS WHOSE AIM IS TO BRING DOWN THE REPUBLIC' An official close to Interior Minister Laurent Nuñez said that by early Thursday, around 270,000 people had joined the union action in 180 rallies outside the capital. About a third of France’s high schools were closed or unable to operate, some because of student blockades and others because teachers were on strike, The Associated Press reported. Toby Harris, an Australian tourist who was visiting Paris on Thursday, told Fox News Digital that "I feel like it's probably a good thing that there's like political action in the city. items.summary_original: Multiple planes across Europe were diverted and forced to make emergency landings Thursday because of bomb threats that have turned out to be unfounded. At least 11 planes, originating from cities including Copenhagen, Dublin, Helsinki, Madrid, Milan and Warsaw, have been affected. The source of the threats was not immediately clear. These incidents came after several flights in Europe received similar warnings on Tuesday that the U.K. government described as "malicious hoax threats." "Upon receiving a threat regarding the placement of an improvised explosive device on board 4 aircraft heading to Prague, we are preparing with colleagues from Prague Airport for their landing. We assess the relevance of the threats as low," Czech Police wrote on X, before adding that inspections of the planes yielded "negative results." The threats come at a time when European officials have been blaming Russia and Iran for "hybrid attacks" and acts of sabotage, which both Moscow and Tehran deny, Reuters reported. That flight landed safely at the base in Evreux in Normandy, with all 151 passengers and six crew members disembarking, the office said. items.summary_original: A U.S. Marine died Tuesday after an incident during training at Camp Schwab in Okinawa, Japan, military officials said. The incident happened in Okinawa, on a Marine Corps base near the northeastern coast of Okinawa Prefecture. The Marine, who was identified as Lance Cpl. Devin J. Hernandez, 25, of Maryland, was with the 3rd Marine Division. "We express our deepest condolences to the family and loved ones of our Marine." Hernandez was participating in fast-rope training at Camp Schwab when he sustained injuries during the training, the 3rd Marine Division said in a later statement to Fox News Digital. He was transported to a hospital and later succumbed to his injuries. "A Marine currently assigned to 3rd Marine Division was involved in a fast rope training incident at Camp Schwab on Nov. 3, 2026. Hannah Ladd said in a statement to Fox News Digital. The Marine's death remains under investigation, the 3rd Marine Division said. items.summary: به گفته مقامات، یک زن کانادایی و دخترش در یک حمله مشکوک خرس گریزلی در آخر هفته هنگام پیاده روی در مسیری نزدیک خانه خود کشته شدند. جنیفر بالکاراس، 48 ساله، هنردرمانگر، و دخترش، سله رید، 20 ساله، روز شنبه پس از رفتن به پیاده روی در مسیر Snooka West Trail، تنها چند دقیقه از خانه خود در بلا کولا، بریتیش کلمبیا، ناپدید شدند. برادرش مت بالکاراس به The Vancouver Sun گفت که وقتی بالکاراس در یک جلسه آنلاین برنامه ریزی شده در روز شنبه حاضر نشد، عزیزان نگران شدند. راهنمای عملی برای اینکه خرس در تابستان امسال در حین پیاده‌روی یا کمپینگ مورد حمله قرار نگیرید پس از اینکه نتوانستند به این جفت برسند، بستگان از پلیس سواره سلطنتی کانادا (RCMP) خواستند تا یک بررسی رفاهی را در صبح یکشنبه انجام دهند. مقامات خودروی بالکاراس را که در آن پارک شده بود کشف کردند
items.summary_original: A Canadian woman and her daughter were killed in a suspected grizzly bear attack over the weekend while hiking on a trail near their home, according to authorities. Jennifer Balcarras, 48, an art therapist, and her daughter, Selah Reed, 20, went missing Saturday after going for a walk on the Snooka West Trail, just minutes from their home in Bella Coola, British Columbia . Loved ones grew concerned when Balcarras failed to show up for a scheduled online meet-up on Saturday, her brother, Matt Balcarras, told The Vancouver Sun . A PRACTICAL GUIDE TO NOT GETTING MAULED BY A BEAR WHILE HIKING OR CAMPING THIS SUMMER After failing to reach the pair, relatives asked the Royal Canadian Mounted Police (RCMP) for a welfare check on Sunday morning. Authorities discovered Balcarras' vehicle parked at the trailhead . Her body was recovered Monday, and search teams found Reed's body on Tuesday. Tyre noted that officers were actively working to "locate and capture any bears involved" and said it was not immediately clear if more than one animal was responsible. items.summary_original: After crushing powerful criminal gangs in El Salvador, President Nayib Bukele has turned his attention to the Caribbean nation of Haiti, deploying 2,000 troops after four Salvadoran military aviation technicians disappeared following an Oct.18 ambush near Port-au-Prince. "We have already finished with the gangs in El Salvador, and we can finish with you too," Bukele wrote in a message on X directed at Haiti's criminal groups. Bukele stressed that the operation's objective was not to invade Haiti or conduct a long-term occupation, but to recover the four missing Salvadorans alive. The disappearance has become a national priority for Bukele, who has warned Haitian gang leaders that El Salvador is prepared to use overwhelming force if the men are not returned alive. Haiti’s National Police announced Tuesday, more than two weeks after the attack, that it had found the charred remains of the vehicle in the Santo neighborhood of Croix-des-Bouquets. Police said, however, they found no sign of the missing men. El Salvador says the men were abducted, the Haitian government says the soldiers are missing, and one gang leader says they are dead. The final vote count, published last Friday by Israel's Central Elections Committee, gave Netanyahu's bloc 53 seats in the 120-member Knesset, compared with 48 for the opposition alliance led by Gadi Eisenkot — 61 seats are needed to form a government. On Monday, Netanyahu posted to X that "the public in Israel does not want a government that depends on Ra'am and the Joint List—parties that support terrorism and reject the existence of the Jewish state." NETANYAHU DEFIES EXIT POLLS AS VOTE SHIFTS IN HIS FAVOR, BUT MAJORITY REMAINS ELUSIVE "A clear majority in the Jewish public chose the Likud as the largest party and me, as prime minister, to lead the next government. We aspire to form a broad government with our partners and with any party that wishes to do so and does not support terrorism. I am open to holding discussions on the matter," he added. The two predominantly Arab parties he pointed his criticism at are the Joint List and Ra'am who secured a historic combined total of 19 seats, potentially positioning them as kingmakers in the government formation process. items.summary_original: KYIV, Ukraine — Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy is defying calls from the Trump administration for his armed forces to stop attacking Russian oil refineries, telling Fox News: "Our response must be painful." In an interview in Kyiv, Zelenskyy acknowledged holding discussions with the Trump administration about targeting oil facilities, attacks President Donald Trump has pinned as being partly to blame for high gas prices in the U.S. "We had different conversations — different, and several — with President Trump and with his team about attacks on refineries," Zelenskyy said. "We said that if you want us not to attack Russia's refineries, they have not to attack our energy system." TRUMP TELLS ZELENSKYY TO STOP DOING 'ONE THING' DURING ATTACKS ON RUSSIA Ukraine has reported near-daily Russian strikes on energy infrastructure , triggering power outages just as temperatures dip ahead of winter. "That's why we have to respond. But our response has to be painful for Russian military people," Zelenskyy said. "If we will not respond on energy, they will continue." U.S.-Ukraine relations took a further hit in October when Trump struck a deal to import millions of tons of Russian diesel to the United States. items.summary_original: U.S. officials will mediate a new round of talks between Ukraine and Russia next week with the goal of delivering "lasting security for generations to come," U.S. Special Envoy Steve Witkoff said on Monday. Witkoff said the U.S.-mediated negotiations will be held on Nov. 10 and 11 in Abu Dhabi in the United Arab Emirates. "The United States will mediate working-level negotiations between Ukraine and Russia on November 10–11 in Abu Dhabi, advancing President Trump’s mission to end the war. Discussions will focus on post-war security arrangements, de-escalation, humanitarian efforts, and next steps toward peace," Witkoff wrote on X. INSIDE MELANIA TRUMP'S SECRET DIPLOMATIC ROLE IN THE RUSSIA-UKRAINE CEASEFIRE DEAL Ahead of next week's peace talks, U.S. negotiators will meet this week in Brussels with representatives from France, Germany, the United Kingdom, the EU and NATO. "Additionally, American negotiators will meet this week in Brussels with representatives from France, Germany, the United Kingdom, the EU, and NATO to discuss security guarantees for Ukraine, Europe’s post-war security architecture, and economic opportunities to support Ukraine’s reconstruction," Witkoff said. The Ukrainian leader's warning came as voters prepared to decide which party controls Congress, a result that could also influence Washington's future response to Russian President Vladimir Putin's almost five-year war in Ukraine. In a post on X, Zelenskyy went on to urge the Trump administration to increase pressure on Moscow, warning that Russia could exploit the elections to target Ukraine's battered energy infrastructure and supply routes. DRONE STRIKE SINKS SHIP IN NATO WATERS AS ZELENSKYY WARNS OF LOOMING ‘MASSIVE STRIKE’ "We have intel that Russia is preparing a new massive attack on our country – primarily targeting energy and logistics," Zelenskyy said in his nightly address. "The assumption is basically that tomorrow the world will be watching the American midterms, and what is happening here in Ukraine, along with our difficulties with air defense and Patriot missiles, will be overlooked." Zelenskyy's warning came hours after Russian forces struck a school being used to distribute humanitarian aid in Komyshuvakha, a settlement in southeastern Ukraine's Zaporizhzhia region. items.summary_original: Friday’s late-night confrontation at Poland's Constitutional Tribunal, which drew riot police and protesters and prompted President Karol Nawrocki to turn his plane around and return to Warsaw, has reignited a bitter debate over whether Prime Minister Donald Tusk is restoring the rule of law or overstepping constitutional limits. The dispute erupted after the tribunal announced the suspension of its president, Bogdan Święczkowski, a move that supporters of Tusk’s government described as necessary to restore judicial independence, while critics denounced it as an unconstitutional power grab. Marcin Przydacz, the head of the International Policy Bureau in Nawrocki’s office, took to European TV Monday morning denouncing Tusk’s actions, saying, "Even lawyers who are close to the Tusk government say that there's absolutely no legal basis for such behavior." POLISH PRESIDENT TURNS PLANE AROUND AFTER 'COUP' AT NATION’S TOP COURT The dispute is also triggering diplomatic fallout, with at least three Polish ambassadors resigning in protest. Przydacz, a former parliament member of the now-opposition Law and Justice (PiS) party, says Poland’s permanent representative to the U.N. since 2021, Krzysztof Szczerski, resigned Monday, which followed the resignations over the weekend of the ambassadors to China and Romania. items.summary_original: Ukraine officials said the country’s official air-raid alert app was likely hacked after emergency alerts warned on Sunday that there was a "radiation hazard" and a "chemical attack alert" in Kyiv. The false warnings urged residents not to go outside. "There is a radiation hazard alert in Kyiv. Do not go outside!" read one alert. RUSSIA LAUNCHES BALLISTIC MISSILE ATTACK ON KYIV HOURS AFTER ZELENSKYY WARNS OF MAJOR STRIKE "There is a chemical attack alert in Kyiv. Do not go outside!" another one read. The public air alert online map also displayed Kyiv and other areas as under a nuclear alert. The app also issued false warnings about Russia’s hypersonic Oreshnik missile and alleged street fighting in Kyiv. Additionally, loudspeakers in the streets blasted a recorded message instructing people to take precautions. But Ukraine’s Air Force said its air alert app was hacked and that there was no radiation hazard to be concerned about. "The air alert app appears to have been subjected to enemy influence. There is no radiation threat! Stay calm and follow our updates on our channel!" the Ukrainian Air Force said in a statement posted to Telegram. Ukraine’s Center for Strategic Communications blamed Russia for the incident, although no group had publicly claimed responsibility. UANI identified one of the sanctioned tankers as the SOGL. It allegedly escaped the blockade on Sept. 1 carrying approximately 500,000 barrels of Iranian LPG after collecting it at an Iranian port in August. The vessel then traveled thousands of miles to a Malaysian offshore anchorage, where UANI filmed the vessel receiving fuel and other services offshore. The ship then traveled on to China, where the organization said it discharged its Iranian cargo. items.summary_original: President Abelardo de la Espriella means business when it comes to his war against the cartels. Colombia's new president, known by the nickname of "El Tigre." was voted in on a law-and-order ticket and so far his actions in fighting the cartels are seemingly paying dividends — not just in Colombia but in Washington, too. Recently, he arrived at the Barranquilla police command around the early hours of the morning as 587 police officers and soldiers raided 50 locations across the Caribbean port city and its suburbs in Operation Blindaje 360. A few days earlier, domestic Colombian news outlets had widely publicized a recording intercepted by Colombian police of "Keko," the alleged leader of a gang called "Los del Freseo," boasting that de la Espirella had nothing on him. "The Tiger's got nothing. Let him come out, and we'll put lead in him," Keko allegedly said on the recording. Then, before dawn, Colombia's president had tracked him down and was face to face with him, all caught on tape. According to a video released by his presidential office, El Tigre told Keko the gang leader was "a tough guy on the phone… but the look of the fear on his face matched that of his many victims." The sweep ended with 72 arrests. items.summary_original: The U.S. Embassy in Moscow issued a security alert Saturday warning people of a potential "mass casualty event" at the 2 Museum Reserve in Moscow. "The U.S. Embassy in Moscow is aware of a credible threat of a mass casualty event TODAY October 31, at the Tsaritsyno Museum Reserve in Moscow at Dolskaya Ulitsa 1, Moscow, Russia 11569. The U.S. government is coordinating with appropriate Russian authorities on a response," the embassy wrote in a statement. The alert warned people to avoid the Tsaritsyno Museum area and to "stay alert, and avoid crowds." Founded in 1775 as a summer home for Russia's Catherine II, the Tsaritsyno Museum is now a popular tourist attraction in Russia's capital. INSIDE MELANIA TRUMP'S SECRET DIPLOMATIC ROLE IN THE RUSSIA-UKRAINE CEASEFIRE DEAL The museum itself attracted more than 2 million visitors in 2022, Moscow's deputy mayor, Natalya Sergunina, said in 2023. The surrounding grounds, enjoyed by Moscow's local citizens for physical activity and dog walking, get even more foot traffic, according to The Art Newspaper. The U.S. Embassy's alert also included a warning to people in the Moscow area to keep cellphone batteries and other batteries charged, remain aware of surroundings and review a personal security plan. The alert was issued as tensions in the ongoing war between Russia and Ukraine continue to escalate. items.summary_original: The French government is deploying 70,000 police officers to cities across the country as authorities expect a third week of intense anti-government protests to resume Saturday. Demonstrators objecting to rising costs and President Emmanuel Macron's government have engaged in looting and damaging property, prompting the law enforcement surge, according to officials. "Everyone is on deck to ensure an extremely firm response to any trouble," Interior Minister Laurent Nuñez said at a news conference early in the week. At least 150 planned gatherings across the country have been tracked and acknowledged by the Interior Ministry. Videos circulating on social media Saturday appeared to show fresh confrontations as anti-government protests continued across France despite the deployment of 70,000 police officers nationwide. In Paris, video posted to X by journalist Oliya Scootercaster appeared to show an object being thrown toward a group of riot police as officers moved through a street. items.summary_original: FIRST ON FOX: The State Department has hit out strongly against South Africa and some of its politicians, accusing them of putting their people’s lives at risk after two attacks on White farmers believed to be Afrikaners — people of European descent — near Johannesburg. A 50-year-old man was reportedly tortured, and a 55-year-old woman was allegedly beaten to death. items.summary_original: While en route to Senegal, Poland’s President Karol Nawrocki turned his plane around and returned home after police entered Poland's top court, the Constitutional Tribunal, and the tribunal’s president was suspended. "At such a moment, the President must be in Poland," Nawrocki posted on X . "I'm interrupting my flight to Senegal. I'm returning." Police say they secured the Tribunal after dozens of protesters gathered to demonstrate against what they called the wrongful suspension of the top court’s president by the current pro-European government. Police said there were also dangerous objects thrown at officers outside the building. Some protesters outside the court were seen praying, while others held posters reading "Tusk — a symbol of anti-Polish sentiment," "Down with the commies and Tusk’s regime," and "Stop destroying the state." Poland’s top judicial bodies, including the Constitutional Tribunal, have been a major bone of contention between the current pro-European government, led by Prime Minister Donald Tusk, and the main opposition party, national-conservative Law and Justice (PiS), which ruled the country from 2015 to 2023. Critics accuse the PiS of imposing political control over key judicial institutions, with some reforms having led the EU to impose fines on Poland. The completed count, published early Friday by Israel's Central Elections Committee , gave Netanyahu's bloc 53 seats in the 120-member Knesset, compared with 48 for Eisenkot's opposition alliance. The two predominantly Arab parties secured a historic 19 seats, placing them in a potentially decisive position. Netanyahu's Likud emerged as the largest individual party with 27 seats, followed by Eisenkot's Yashar with 21 and former Prime Minister Naftali Bennett's Beyachad with 12. items.title: بی‌طرفی، راستی‌آزمایی و پاسخ‌گویی؛ چرا بی‌بی‌سی فارسی بر این اصول ایستادگی می‌کند؟
items.summary: این مطلب توضیح می‌دهد که چرا بی‌بی‌سی فارسی در یکی از پرتنش‌ترین دوره‌های تاریخ معاصر ایران بر اصول بنیادین روزنامه‌نگاری، از جمله بی‌طرفی، راستی‌آزمایی، استقلال تحریریه و پاسخ‌گویی، پافشاری می‌کند. در این مقاله، با مرور شیوه تصمیم‌گیری‌های تحریریه، فرآیند راستی‌آزمایی اخبار، نحوه انتخاب مهمانان و برخورد با خطاها و انتقادها، تشریح می‌شود که هدف بی‌بی‌سی نه جانبداری از هیچ طرف، بلکه ارائه گزارشی دقیق، مستقل و مبتنی بر شواهد است تا مخاطبان بتوانند بر اساس اطلاعات قابل اعتماد، خود درباره رویدادها قضاوت کنند.
